theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: SEPARATED_COMMUTATION
theorems.statement: two local mechanics with distinct write coordinates, neither reading what the other writes, commute on any state over any value domain, for every transformer obeying its declared frame
theorems.why_it_matters: the finite core checks this for four binary coordinates and one modular transformer; against an arbitrary transformer the result can only be a property of separation rather than of the arithmetic that instantiated it

theorems.detail: a disagreeing model exists, so separation is not merely sufficient
theorems.name: SEPARATION_IS_NECESSARY
theorems.statement: if one mechanic reads the coordinate the other writes, commutation is not entailed: there is a state and a pair of frame-respecting transformers whose two orders disagree
theorems.why_it_matters: states the converse, so separation is reported as the boundary it is and not as one sufficient condition among unnamed others

theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: WRITE_LOCALITY
theorems.statement: a local mechanic changes its own write coordinate and no other
theorems.why_it_matters: the soundness half: a mechanic declared local must actually be local, or every separation argument built on the declaration is void

theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: FRAME_DETERMINACY
theorems.statement: two states agreeing on a mechanic's declared frame produce the same written value, so nothing outside the frame can influence the result
theorems.why_it_matters: the minimality half: the declared read set is the whole dependency, which is what makes a dependency graph a description of the computation rather than a comment on it

theorems.detail: negation is unsatisfiable under the axioms
theorems.name: IDEMPOTENT_ON_FIXPOINT
theorems.statement: a mechanic that leaves its state unchanged leaves it unchanged when reapplied
theorems.why_it_matters: the conservativity half: reapplying a settled mechanic cannot manufacture a change, so a fixpoint is a real stopping condition

what_this_establishes: separated commutation, write locality, frame determinacy and fixpoint conservativity hold for any number of coordinates over any value domain and for every transformer obeying its declared frame; and P6's committed mechanic obeys its declared frame, so the bounded enumeration in check_finite_models is an instance of the general result rather than a separate finding
